title: Checkout service explorer
lede: A small web checkout traced end to end. Pick a flow, select a component, or open the timeline. Dotted terms open a definition in place.

web.name: Web app
web.role: Cart, checkout form and order status page.
details: Sends an idempotency key with every payment request so a double click cannot charge twice.
qs: How should the client retry a payment request that timed out?

gateway.name: API gateway
gateway.role: TLS, auth token validation, rate limits and routing.
risks: One shared gateway is one shared failure; config changes need code-level review.
qs: What belongs in the gateway versus the service?

orders.name: Order service
orders.role: Creates orders, reserves stock and asks for payment.

details.t: Uses an outbox table so the order row and its event commit together.
more: The event is written in the same transaction as the order, and a relay publishes it afterwards.
No lost events if the broker is down.
details.code:
INSERT INTO orders ...;
INSERT INTO outbox (topic, payload) VALUES ('order.created', ...);

risks: Stock reserved but payment never completes: needs a reservation expiry.
qs: Why an outbox instead of publishing directly?
How long should a stock reservation last?

payments.name: Payment service
payments.role: Talks to the payment processor; the only place card tokens are handled.
details: Calls are idempotent on the client's idempotency key.
qs: How do you reconcile with the processor's records?

db.name: Orders DB
db.role: System of record for orders and the outbox.

bus.name: Event bus
bus.role: Carries order.created and payment.captured to other teams.

flows.name: Place an order
flows.intro: From pressing Buy to a confirmed order.
steps: Submit checkout with an idempotency key
Order row and outbox event written in one transaction

flows.name: Retry after timeout
flows.intro: The client never saw a response and tries again.
steps: Key already seen: load the stored result
Original result returned, no second charge

idem.d: A client-chosen id sent with a request so the server can recognise a repeat and return the first result instead of acting twice.

outbox.d: Events are written to a table in the same transaction as the data change, then published by a relay. The event exists if and only if the change committed.

timeline.intro: A sample incident, minute by minute. Timelines work on any scale: years, quarters, sprints or seconds.

events.title: On-call paged
events.what: Alert fires on the error budget burn rate.

events.title: Duplicate charge reports
events.what: Clients retried without an idempotency key.
events.why: Shows why every payment call needs one.

events.title: Key enforced at the gateway
events.what: Requests without an idempotency key are rejected.

topics.title: Retries: safe repeats without double effects
topics.summary: Clients retry on timeouts, so every write must be idempotent.
points: Generate the idempotency key once per user intent, not per attempt.
Store the first result keyed by the idempotency key.

notes.label: Interview angle
notes.text: Explain where the key is stored and for how long.

ask.context: The reader is learning how a web checkout handles orders and payments reliably.
ask.style: Answer as a senior engineer with concrete mechanisms and tradeoffs. Plain text, under 200 words.
